### D3 red team · Question

Event: `741ce9998ebc1dfef706395b714b1dea` · 2026-09-24T21:20:43Z

> D3 code review, checkpoint 2 (netd). Read in the scratch worktree /tmp/d3cr1, detached at f29322646; the implementer's tree was not touched. I read every non-fake source file line by line. Baseline: `cargo test -p redoubt-netd`, 13 + 7 passed. Release builds for rv64 and rv32 pass. I planted 25 bugs one at a time, each reverted afterwards; the scratch tree is clean.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes. Two P2s, neither blocking this checkpoint; the second must close with the libs/rt commit.
> 
> == Device lies: every device value is checked before use ==
> - Used idx: `used_since` takes idx.wrapping_sub(next_used) and refuses more than the outstanding count, so a jump, a step back (which wraps large) or completions never offered are all a Lie.
> - Entries are read at netd's own counter, `counter % 16`. A u16 wraps cleanly because 16 divides 65536.
> - Ids: must be below 16 and outstanding. The bit is cleared as each entry is checked, and slots are re-offered only after the whole batch, so a duplicate within one batch is caught (dup-id mutant caught).
> - Length: rx must be in 12..=2048, otherwise a Lie, checked before `scratch[..len]`. tx must be at most 2048.
> - Header: flags == 0 and gso_type == 0, read from netd's copy, not from DMA.
> - Frames of 14..1514 are delivered; any other length within the slot is dropped and counted, never a Lie.
> - QueueNumMax is only compared. A queue already READY is refused, and QUEUE_READY is read back.
> - MAC: read bytewise under ConfigGeneration with 8 tries, and zero, multicast or broadcast is refused.
> - Features: exactly VERSION_1 and MAC are written, with FEATURES_OK and the FAILED/NEEDS_RESET bits checked on every status write.
> - No device value is ever used as an index, length or address: every descriptor address is `phys_of(dma_phys, slot_off(i))` with a checked add, and the queue bases are phys plus a constant.
> 
> == Tables and avail ring are never read back ==
> They are written through dma_write, and no read of DESC_OFF or AVAIL_OFF exists. write_desc rewrites the whole descriptor on every offer and every transmit. publish rewrites avail.flags and idx from netd's own counters. `configure` zeroes both rings before QUEUE_READY.
> 
> == Copy-once, zeroing, TX length ==
> - rx: `dma_read(slot_off(id), &mut scratch[..len])`; every check and delivery then uses the copy. Each slot is zeroed (dma_zero of 2048 bytes) before it is re-offered.
> - tx: the descriptor length is exactly 12 + frame.len(). The fake counts any read past it (overread) and the test asserts the wire bytes.
> - Mutants caught: no-zero (the inflated-length test) and tx-len = SLOT_LEN (the exact-transmit test).
> 
> == Hand-over, BROKEN, client badge ==
> - Both regions are allocated, both queues configured, rx offered and DRIVER_OK set by the serving thread before thread_create.
> - RxPart goes through `AtomicPtr` swap plus `Box::into_raw`/`from_raw`, taken exactly once. A failed thread_create reclaims and drops it, and the caller resets.
> - No message carries an address: the only send from the rx thread is `[BROKEN,0,0,0]` with no handles and no buffer, on a minted badge `1<<63 | random`.
> - The serving thread acts only on words[0]==BROKEN from that exact badge. max_transfer is 0, handles on any send are closed, and a send has no other effect.
> - `parse_client`: exactly one argument, decimal, no leading zero, nonzero and below 2^63, so it can never equal the BROKEN badge.
> - dispatch: any badge other than the client, or any label, gets not_permitted before the device is touched; broken gets failed. Mutants on labels, badge, client63 and broken-serves were all caught.
> 
> == Never exits on a device fault; reset on controlled exits ==
> - A bring_up failure resets and serves `failed`.
> - A Lie or Timeout in transmit triggers break_device, which resets once.
> - An rx lie resets, reports and ends the thread.
> - start_receiving failing (random or stack) resets, then exits with NO_RESOURCES, which is a resource fault, not a device fault.
> - The loop ending (Dead or receive failure) resets, then exits.
> - Mutants caught: no-reset-on-fail, break-no-reset, tx-timeout.
> 
> P2-1. The rx thread leaves its loop silently. In receive_frames, `wait_irq` returning Err(Kernel) does `return` with no reset and no BROKEN report. The device stays DRIVER_OK with 16 rx buffers armed, transmit keeps succeeding, and ipd receives nothing, never told. That breaks the plan's 'either thread leaving its loop resets'. Fix: every exit from receive_frames resets the device and sends BROKEN, and the serving thread answers failed from then on. Put it in lib code so a host test can drive it.
> 
> P2-2. The panic hook isn't wired yet. f29322646's message says 'the panic path joins with the runtime's panic hook', but nothing in netd or libs/rt calls set_panic_hook at this commit. It must land in the libs/rt commit, with netd storing the register base before bring-up, and with a test (checkpoint 3). Until then a netd panic leaves the device armed; that is covered by the no-restart gate, but the claim in the message is ahead of the code.
> 
> == The 7 unsafe blocks (kernel.rs; budget max_unsafe = 7, undocumented 0) ==
> - reg_read, reg_read_u8 and reg_write go through `Regs::at`, which checks alignment, `off + width <= len` with a checked add, and `base + off` with a checked add.
> - dma_read, dma_write and dma_zero go through `dma_at`, checked against REGION_LEN, byte-wise volatile, so no &[u8] over device memory exists.
> - take_rx_part: the swap guarantees a single owner.
> The SAFETY comments are accurate. The mappings are never unmapped because Device holds raw usizes with no Drop, which is right while the device may DMA. Minor: `start_rx_thread` only debug_asserts that the previous pointer was null; in release a second call would leak the first part. That's harmless, since the program calls it once.
> 
> == K5b constraint: no DMA page is ever lent, transferred or process_map'd ==
> The only Buffer sent is `Buffer::new(1)`, an anonymous page, filled by encoding the frame from `scratch`, which is netd's stack. `transmit` copies out of the caller's lend into the slot. Replies carry no buffer. There is no process_map anywhere in the crate. DMA addresses exist only as usize and phys values inside Device.
> 
> == Would the tests catch regressions? Mostly yes ==
> Caught: dup-id, no-zero, tx-len, badlen-as-lie, header flags, gso, rx min length, tx outstanding, labels, badge, client63, broken-serves, features written, MAC unicast, version, tx timeout, reset on failed bring-up, break without reset, QUEUE_READY live, ConfigGeneration.
> Survived:
> - (a) `fresh > 16` instead of `> outstanding`: equivalent, because the outstanding-bit check refuses the surplus entry anyway.
> - (b) FEATURES_OK not re-checked: equivalent, because set_status reads the same bit back.
> - (c) rx descriptors not rewritten on re-offer: NOT caught. The scribble test sends one frame after scribbling. Add a case with a scribble, then an honest policy, then N frames that must all arrive, so the documented 'written whole every time' property is tested.
> - (d) next_used non-wrapping (`+ 1`): NOT caught. exercise() runs at most 8 rounds, so no test ever wraps a u16 counter. Release wraps silently, but the checked profile (overflow-checks) would panic after 65,536 frames. Add a host test that pushes more than 65,552 frames and transmits through both queues. That is cheap on the host.
> 
> The bin's event loop (BROKEN-badge match, send drop) has no host test. Moving it into lib, as ipd's dispatch does, would let tests cover it.
> 
> == Fuzz ==
> Acceptable for this checkpoint. Both fuzz targets' bodies are the host sweeps: `fake::exercise` is shared with `randomized_hostile_devices`, 20,000 seeded devices asserting strayed == crossed == overread == 0 and no panic; the request target is the server sweep. What coverage-guided fuzzing adds is depth: long sequences and wrap, which (d) shows is missing. Conditions: add the wrap test now, and make a cargo-fuzz run of both targets a retained gate before netd is used off the bench (it already waits for K5b). Record that in netd-host-tests or STATUS.
> 
> Scope: only servers/netd, tests/*.toml, unsafe-budget, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock were touched. No kernel/, model/ or K5 paths.

> Fuzz addendum: cargo-fuzz is installed now, so I ran both targets myself in the scratch worktree /tmp/d3cr1 at f29322646, with corpora in /tmp/netdfuzz and the committed seeds. Commands: `cargo +nightly fuzz build` (ok), then `cargo +nightly fuzz run <t> /tmp/netdfuzz/<t> fuzz/seeds/<t> -- -max_total_time=240 -print_final_stats=1`. Results:
> - **device:** 83,649 runs in 241 s, no crash, no ASan or leak report, exit 0. Coverage 841 edges and 2,342 features, 507 new units, final corpus 214 inputs (21 KB). The rate fell from about 3,700 to 347 exec/s as inputs grew to about 376 bytes. RSS rose to 1,050 MB, then flattened from about 23k runs on. That looks like ASan's quarantine plus shadow memory, not a leak, since LeakSanitizer reported nothing, but it is about half of libFuzzer's default 2 GB rss_limit. For long runs, watch it or pass -rss_limit_mb explicitly.
> - **request:** 8,485,845 runs in 241 s (about 35k exec/s), no crash, exit 0. Coverage 294 edges and 584 features, 392 new units, peak RSS 365 MB.
>
